And now that I have come to the end of my humble discourse, let us pray for peace, rest, and eternal glory for our good Superior; not because I fear, and you with me suspect, that her holy soul does not yet enjoy the beatific vision of God and needs our prayers; but because the Church so wills it, nor do I mean to anticipate her judgments: O Saints of the heavenly Zion, come to meet Sister A. del Salvatore, and you, Angels of the Lord, receiving her soul, present it before the Most High. May Christ receive you, who chose you as his beloved virgin, and may the Angels lead you into the bosom of Abraham. Peace, eternal blessedness to you, O Sister Anna del Salvatore; while we, to whom you left a precious legacy of virtue, will strive to follow in your footsteps, and to live as you lived, so as to die with the precious death of the Saints, with which you completed your mortal pilgrimage here below.

3. Article in "La Sicilia Cattolica" on the solemn funeral of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, year XVIII, no. 132, June 15-16, 1885, unsigned (Proc. p. 506).

It recounts the solemn obsequies celebrated for the Servant of God a week after her death, in the Institute's chapel, with the participation of many sisters and numerous Palermo personalities. The article admiringly recalls the virtues of Sister Anna del Salvatore, especially underscoring her humility, her charity towards the sick and suffering, and her prudence in governance.

Solemn funeral

With a most kind and pious thought, solemn obsequies were celebrated this morning [June 15] for the virtuous and lamented Provincial Superior of the Daughters of St. Anne, in the Oratory of the Central House for Sicily, within the Briuccia Palace.

The said Oratory, and the large hall preceding it, were for the occasion elegantly transformed into a funeral chapel, the vaults draped in mourning, mournful veils fluttering on the walls. At the entrance to the Oratory and all around, one could read most graceful inscriptions recalling the outstanding and singular virtues of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, and in the center stood a magnificent urn of velvet and gold, with a photographic portrait of the deceased, upon whose steps various wreaths had been placed, from the Daughters of St. Anne of the Asylum, from those of the Hospital, from those of the Fernandez Infirmary, etc.

One entered that Oratory, and an arcane and mysterious feeling of sorrow and joy, of death and paradise, searched the very fibers of one's being... and those desolate Daughters, weeping around their Mother's coffin; and those noble and pious Palermo ladies, present there to pay their final tribute of admiration to one so dear to them... and the whole mournful arrangement — one could not say for certain whether it turned the mind more to the suffering misfortune, or to heaven, where an angel had flown to pray before God's throne for the Daughters, for the Institute, for Palermo, for the wretched who languished, who were in this vale of exile her special delight, and for whom she had a mother's heart, a seraph's charity, the living, burning, boundless charity of Christianity and its great institutions.

A great number of Masses were celebrated throughout the day in suffrage for the deceased Provincial Superior; and the solemn canonical Requiem Mass was sung by Msgr. Ignazio Zuccaro, secretary to His Eminence the Cardinal Archbishop of Palermo, through whose efforts the blessed Institution of the Daughters of St. Anne was established among us, and does so much good, and promises the finest fruits for the future as well.

The funeral eulogy was read by the Beneficiary canon Gaetano Gabriele, who delicately managed to show the manifold virtues of Sister Anna del Salvatore from the angle of the chief among virtues, humility, which inspired her in various ways, so pleasing God, and making herself a guide, comfort, and relief for humanity.

The death of the Provincial Superior was a true loss... Of this type of woman and Christian virgin, who loves and prays, who smiles and consumes herself in penance, prudent in governance and loving in guidance, who has the innocence of the dove and the energy of the strong woman, who lives not for herself but for the suffering members of the mystical body of Jesus Christ. Who did not see her, and love her, and esteem her, and was not captivated by her virtue and her manner?

Blessed one! Your daughters will not forget you, this city will not forget you... and pray you for us all!

4. Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi and the Institution of the Daughters of St. Anne, in "La Sicilia Cattolica," year XX, no. 39, February 18, 1887, unsigned (Proc. p. 517)

The article recounts the rite of exhumation and the canonical identification of the Servant of God's body; her virtues and her reputation for holiness are recalled. The author praises the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne and its Foundress, Rosa Gattorno, who was present at the ceremony.

Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi and the Institution of the Daughters of St. Anne

On the 14th, at the cemetery of St. Ursula, a sad yet at the same time consoling ceremony took place.

Readers will recall, as the city of Palermo recalls, that in June 1885 the blessed soul of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, Provincial of the worthy Daughters of St. Anne, passed to eternal rest. Her death was received with great anguish by all who knew her, and a spontaneous cry was heard everywhere: "A saint has died!"

This outcry was taken up by the priests who had known her closely, by the families fortunate enough to have frequent contact with her; so that all formally entreated our venerated Cardinal Archbishop that, mindful of the deceased's virtues, he order her body placed in a deposit, awaiting the Lord's later manifestation of the works of his omnipotence.

Our Pastor, without the slightest hesitation, kindly granted this request, and, considering the blameless life of the good religious, ordered that her remains be kept in a deposit, in accordance with the prescriptions of the Holy Roman Church.

And it was at the cemetery of St. Ursula that this sacred ceremony was to take place. A moving scene! Around the tomb, from which the blessed deceased was to be exhumed, stood: His Most Reverend Excellency Msgr. Giovanni Cirino, Archbishop of Ancyra and Vicar General of the Archdiocese of Palermo, Msgr. Ignazio Zuccaro, through whose zealous work we have the Daughters of St. Anne among us, the Most Reverend Canon Antonino Calì, Chancellor of the Curia, and many priests. Present as well was a numerous group of Daughters of St. Anne, accompanied by their venerable Foundress and Mother General, who had come expressly from Rome to attest her affection for the deceased's virtues; and at Mother General's sides were the Princess of Fitalia and one of the Misses Sorrentino.

We cannot put into words the emotion felt at the moment the coffin containing the good religious's remains was uncovered. It was weeping mixed with joy! Around those bare bones, the good Sisters recognized their Superior, who had so edified them by her humble and mortified life; and they recalled, extolling them, her singular virtues, and her tireless zeal for the salvation of souls, and could not keep from exclaiming: "She was a saint!" Happy to be able to kiss that hand which had so often blessed them, they could not look at her enough... and their rosary beads, and the little crucifixes they wore at their sides, were pressed upon the blessed corpse, as though to receive from it some arcane and superhuman power, in the laborious yet sweet exercise of their Institute's Christian love.

Once the identification of the body was completed, it was, together with a parchment (on which the Most Reverend Fr. Domenico Pizzoli, parish priest of St. Nicholas of the Albergheria, had concisely written the story of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi's life), enclosed in a new coffin with the archiepiscopal seals, and of all this a proper record was drawn up. The sad ceremony ended with the unbloody sacrifice of the Mass, celebrated by the Most Reverend parish priest Palazzotto, which those present devoutly attended.

Blessed Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, which already presents us with the first fruits of its virtue and holiness! It is certainly providential in our day, and we are glad to seize this occasion, which has brought Mother General to Palermo, to attest to her, together with our own, the applause and blessings of religion and civil society.

The noble lady, Countess [sic] Rosa Gattorno, well understood that woman is made for the great struggles that human nature wages against suffering. She therefore set her heart on the blessed Institute, and, leaving behind the splendors of her house, gave herself to the work! And here are the Daughters of St. Anne, in whom the feminine fiber seems to be tempered into strength; and the defenseless creature, made manfully bold, grows great in courage amid dangers, advances spiritedly in the battles of life, dies with fortitude, gloriously, before the hardest trials. Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi is a noble example and eloquent witness of this. Was she not a victim of her own charity?

Even today, the newspaper titled the Italian Army warmly salutes "the angelic Daughters of St. Anne" who have gone to the inhospitable lands of Africa. And we would add that they, like soldiers, have a uniform; like combatants, a weapon, the cross; like warriors, a discipline: but if the soldier fights the enemy for the honor of the flag, for the glory his fellow citizens will pay him when, returning victorious, they receive him in triumph, crown him with laurel, shower fragrant flowers by the handful upon his path; ah! these women aspire to no glory on this earth, they have no enemies but human ailments to cure, they consecrate themselves for brothers who speak the same language as they do, sacrificing themselves also for all whom Jesus Christ has redeemed, for all upon whose brow shines the mark of an immortal soul, because they are the soldiers of humanity.

Blessed Daughters of St. Anne! Most noble is the enterprise of charity, the great and sublime idea that God himself brought to earth. If the world sometimes despises you — that world whose perfidy the unhappy Leopardi understood so well, and noted to be in keeping with what the Gospel says of it... ah! heed not the voices of men, but draw your inspiration rather from the magnanimous examples, from the virtues of your Institute. From Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi; let those who succumb under hard trials be succeeded by others as placid and serene as the spirit of charity.

From high heaven, the Most High God will bless so many sacrifices and so much heroism, and will mark your Institute with the stamp of holiness.

Let us pray the Lord to be pleased to glorify his faithful servant, Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi!

5. Chronicle of the translation of the Servant of God's mortal remains, October 28, 1957: "A Date to Remember," in "Virga Jesse," XXIV (1957), no. 4 (Proc. p. 528).

On the afternoon of Monday, October 28, 1957, at the cemetery of St. Ursula in this city of Palermo, the translation of the Sacred Remains of the venerated Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, the first Provincial of Sicily, took place, from the old tomb at the edge of the cemetery itself, to a specially prepared marble sarcophagus in the family chapel of the Daughters of St. Anne.

Already from the early afternoon hours, a crowded group of Sisters hovered around the chapel; the cheerful look on each face, and the Sisters' hushed chatter, stood in evident contrast with the austerity of the place, and it seemed as though the cypresses, soaring into the cloudy autumn sky, were also whispering something to the wind, as if astonished at such unusual behavior!

It is exactly 3 p.m., and the ecclesiastical authorities arrive: Msgr. Cambria, Chancellor of the Archiepiscopal Curia, together with another priest assisting him, two surgeon doctors, Dr. Iacono and Dr. Speciale, for the examination of each bone, two photographers, and other officials of the cemetery, who will take part in the work to be done. Also present among the Sisters are the Reverend Provincial Sister Anna Franca Medulla, two of her Assistants, and other Superiors of the houses of Palermo and Monreale.

The chapel at once seems smaller than it really is, holding so great a number of persons; everyone wants to see, and each would like to be in the front row!

The small box containing the Sacred Remains had already, for some months, been in the family chapel, by express will of the Archiepiscopal Curia, which, wishing to arrange more fittingly the old tomb where Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi had lain since her death on June 7, 1885, expressed its authoritative opinion that the said tomb should be done away with, as being in an unworthy place; indeed, the ravine underneath, which bred mosquitoes and flies, as well as the stench of rotting garlands and flowers that were dumped just behind the boundary wall, amounted to a considerable disgrace.

The Reverend Mother General, informed by Provincial Superior Medulla in a venerated letter of August 24 of this year, replied that she not only had no objection, but was most pleased to second the thinking of the Venerated Curia, precisely because this concerns a "Sacred Deposit," as the seals attest, placed a first time in 1887 by Cardinal Celesia, barely two years after the Servant of God's death, and in 1932 by Cardinal Lavitrano, following another arrangement of the tomb, made necessary by the flood that at that time damaged the venerated Remains.

Before proceeding to open the coffin, Msgr. Cambria reads the ritual for the ceremony, has the two doctors swear an oath to act in good conscience, warns all those present to observe the most absolute silence and to remove nothing, under pain of excommunication, then orders the work to begin.

The Provincial Superior claims for herself the honor of lifting the dear burden: she takes the small box, lays it on the table already prepared, and, with the help of a pair of scissors, pries loose the pieces of the wooden box, already ruined by damp; the zinc box is thus freed, and at first glance appears to be in good condition.

The Reverend Monsignor Chancellor, the priest, and the doctors argue at length, since it seems to them pointless to move the bones into a new box, when the old one could be placed as it is into the sarcophagus, but... they are all disappointed! The Provincial looks on, agrees to what the Authority wishes to do, but... she is not convinced: the box is all dirty, stained, and in some spots rather corroded. So she asks at least leave to clean it, and is permitted to use a wad of cotton soaked in alcohol.

It is done; but Sister Anna del Salvatore wished to grant us the pleasure of seeing her bones, and let the Provincial see first one little hole, then another, then still another, and then... "let it be opened," decides Monsignor Cambria!

In less time than it takes to tell, the box is open, and to the eyes peering trembling within, there appears a large half-wrapped bundle and those blessed bones that honor us so greatly!

One by one, while the Provincial holds the new zinc box, a Sister wearing gloves takes up and lays down the bones, while the two doctors count them and call out their scientific names: ribs, vertebrae, humerus, ulna, radius, femur, frontal bone, jawbone with embedded teeth, tarsus, metatarsus, phalanges, etc.

The secretary priest writes up the record, which will be duly signed by the responsible authorities, and then deposited in the Archives of the Archiepiscopal Curia; meanwhile, the Provincial Superior lays over the venerated bones, to cover them properly, a small linen cloth, and invites all those present to place a devout kiss, before closing and sealing the box.

The moment is truly moving: it is a veritable contest of love: not only is that dear treasure kissed, but foreheads are rested upon it to obtain a blessing, rosaries, crucifixes, medals, and whatever each one has with her are laid upon it; one nurse, bolder than the others, presses upon it a long skein of gauze and a few packets of cotton, which she then jealously carries off with her, to use with the sick.

When all those present have satisfied their devotion, the box is soldered shut, bound with galvanized wire and a sturdy ribbon, on whose knots the seals of the Archiepiscopal Curia are affixed; it is then lowered into the sarcophagus, and the heavy lid, topped with a cross, is placed over it.

Now Sister Anna del Salvatore is there, in her "Sacred Deposit," from which she follows our work, watches over the dangers we meet, upholds our sometimes wavering courage, and points out to us the path of perfect observance and holiness.

All the Daughters of St. Anne in the Institute may picture her in her marble tomb, but they have the duty of following her heroic example, of imitating her outstanding virtues, of praying to her fervently to seek her intercession and obtain for us an abundant supply of graces; this great Sister must be felt alive among us, to rekindle our religious enthusiasm and the sense of veneration that, alas, is so lacking today!

May Sister Anna del Salvatore come out a little from her humble silence, and shine upon all the Daughters of St. Anne the heavenly light she enjoys in the peace of the Saints, and may she stir up, with renewed fervor, a new era, that of the holiness of the Daughters of St. Anne!

So be it!

Sister Daughter of St. Anne

a) Reports of graces received through the intercession of the Servant of God

A selection of documents and reports is presented here concerning graces obtained through the intercession of the Servant of God (mostly cures and particular help), which fully develop the references already contained in the previous process "Reports" on the virtues and reputation for holiness of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi (cf. supra, p. 312).

1. Letter of Sister Anna Costanza Cenni, of 6/26/1886, Trapani (AFSA C.3.163).

At the express wish of the Foundress, Mother Rosa Gattorno, some graces obtained through the intercession of Sister Anna del Salvatore are recounted to Superior Sister A. Battistina.

Dearest Superior,

I am replying to your letter of the 16th of this month, in which I learned that you wish to have a detailed account of the graces obtained through the intercession of the fortunate soul of A. Salvatore:

The first, then, was the one received by Sister A. Stimate, who was suffering from her right eye, and was treated for several days by Doctor Eugenio Scio. Witnesses of the miracle are Sister A. Costanza and Sister A. Oliveto, who indeed applied the photograph to her.

2. The same Sister A. Stimate, at the start of May, was struck by strong pains in her feet, from which she had already suffered for many years back, and it is so true that even Mother was aware of it, because, knowing how much she had already suffered for some years, she had relieved her of the office of alms-collector. Now, it happened that, since the said Sister had been benefited in her eyes, at the first pains she felt she again turned to the dear departed Sister A. Salvatore, telling her that within that same month she wanted the grace, and indeed, by the end of last May she no longer felt any pain, and, better still, she now stands all day, keeps vigil, and even wears her shoes well, whereas before she could not bear to wear them. So, the grace of the healing of the eye she obtained on April 23, 1886, and that of the feet at the end of May, and the whole community is witness to both.

Sister A. Costanza, for her part, around the middle of April, felt a most acute pain in her throat, where twelve years before she had undergone the operation (which Sister A. Salvatore had treated), and this time too she feared having to undergo some further cutting, for she saw a point that caused her such pain that she could not even sleep. After a day or two, seeing that it would not subside, she thought of placing upon it the photograph of Sister A. Salvatore, and did so; she kept it there all night, and in the morning the pain had completely disappeared, and she never felt it again, and witness to this is Sister A. Oliveto, who was present when she placed the photograph.

Moreover, a girl from Trapani, who lay gravely ill in the hospital, and, to put it better, at death's door, had near her the chaplain of that institution, to prepare her to receive the last Sacraments. The poor girl would have none of it, and whenever the priest drew near, she would turn her back on him. Seeing this, the chaplain withdrew and went to the chapel to give the blessing, since the May devotions were being held, leaving the hospital's Superior near the dying girl. She, remaining there, began to say something to her, but to no avail. Finally the Superior thought to turn to Sister A. Salvatore, and said an Our Father to her, at the end of which she turned to the sick girl and said something to her, and she said: "call me the Father." He went at once, had the May devotions interrupted; the chaplain heard her confession, gave her Viaticum, Extreme Unction, and after three hours this poor girl died.

Father Gagliani too, just a few days ago, wrote that Sister A. Salvatore had worked so many graces for him, and that she truly watches his Company with a kindly eye, and, to venerate her all the more, he has taken her as his protectress and advocate before the Most High, and to honor her still further and never forget her, he had the name of his Company's Superior changed, she who, when she took the habit, was called Sister Melania, and on the day of her profession he had her take the name Sister A. Salvatore.

Now I have nothing more than all this; I have written it to you because this morning Mother wrote to me telling me to write you everything, and for this reason I have delayed until today. Receive my greetings together with those of the whole community, and I remain your most unworthy sister in Jesus.

Sister A. Costanza Cenni

Trapani, 6/26/86

2. Reports on the grace obtained by Mr. Giuseppe Presti, August 1886 (AFSA C. 3. 163).

a. Report of the healed man, undated, to be attributed to August 1886.

He recounts his own illness, which brought him to the point of death, and the rapid cure obtained after praying to the Servant of God and touching one of her relics.

Mr. Giuseppino Presti states that on May 23 he was struck by an infectious fever, which reached 41.5 degrees, with the most acute pains at the tip of the upper femur bone of his left leg, when the patient asked for the doctor at every moment to give him morphine injections and thus ease the pain, but all in vain.

Over a period of 15 days, a certain swelling gradually began to appear on the outside. Most intense fevers accompanied the pain, and neither sulfate of quinine nor its extract were enough to calm the fevers. Prayers were unceasing, novenas to the Most Blessed Virgin of Pompei, triduums; the patient too prayed, but with the most living faith. Finally, after a month of this martyrdom, when the doctors were already despairing of operating, the Queen of Victories seemed to hear him, when the great quantity of matter that had accumulated internally perforated the rectum, and a great amount of blood, matter, and an extraordinary stench began to pass below. After some 8 or 10 days, the sick man began to burn internally, so much so that the doctors, fearing gangrene would set in, decided to make an external incision. On June 16, three surgeons performed the operation, but nothing came out except a foul-smelling gas.

Meanwhile, on June 20, the Most Reverend Father Gaetano Gagliani and the Sisters of Good Hope were going about collecting alms for the hospital, and, passing along that street, were asked to come in, since the sick man desired them greatly. The Most Reverend Canon Gagliani, after exhorting him to have living faith, placed upon his head the veil of Sister Anna [del Salvatore Orsi], who had died in the odor of sanctity. Once this ceremony was over, the Sisters and the Director left, and the patient remained calm, so much so that scarcely had the octave of Corpus Christi ended than he could call himself well. A second grace was that the internal wound healed, not as the doctors said it would leave a fistula, but fully healed, and better than medical art had achieved.

Now the patient finds himself in full convalescence, and never ceases to pay honor and thanks to the Most Blessed Virgin and to the intercessor Sister Anna [del Salvatore].

Giuseppe Presti

Presti Vincenzo, brother

Salvatrice Giardina, witness

Canon Orazio Cassisi, witness

b. Testimony of Canon Gaetano Gagliani and of the Sisters Daughters of Hope on the same cure, of 8/26/1886.

It attests to the healing of Giuseppe Presti, which took place after he received the invitation to pray to Sister Anna del Salvatore and was touched with a relic of the same Servant of God.

I.M.I.

Sicily - Comiso, August 26, 1886

From the Regina Margherita Hospital

I, the undersigned, Canon Gaetano Gagliani, Superior of the Company of the Daughters of Mary Most Holy of Hope, attest the following.

On June 20, 1886, finding myself with a group of Sisters of my Company begging alms in the municipality of Comiso for the poor sick of our Regina Margherita Hospital, I was invited by the Reverend Canon Don Orazio Cassisi to enter the house of the dying Giuseppe Presti, to recite some prayer over him, and comfort him in the final stages of his illness. I entered gladly, accompanied by the Sisters, found him almost at the point of death, and, being a fervent promoter of the glory of the blessed memory of Sister Anna del Salvatore, Provincial of the Daughters of St. Anne, who died in Palermo in the Briuccia Palace, having received from her special and most notable favors, I urged the dying man to place his trust in her, and I applied to his forehead a white linen handkerchief, marked in red with the number 21, which had belonged to blessed Sister Anna, and which, on May 4, 1886, I received as a precious gift, in Palermo, from the Provincial of the Daughters of St. Anne, Sister Anna Battistina. From that moment the sick man felt relief from his excruciating sufferings, improved almost instantly, and, after a few days, left his bed and left the house fully healed.

All this I attest under oath, hand upon breast, in the priestly manner.

Canon Gaetano Gagliani

We, the undersigned, with living affection for Sister Anna del Salvatore, whom we recognize as our mother and Superior, confirm under oath what our Founding Father, Canon Gaetano Gagliani, attests.

Sister Maria Anna del Salvatore Beda

Superior of the Daughters of Hope

Sister Maria Chiara

Assistant

Sister Maria Margherita

Secretary

Sister Maria Geltrude

Treasurer

Sister Maria di Gesù

Nurse

3. Letter of Canon Gaetano Gagliani to Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi, of 8/26/1886 (AFSA C.3.163).

He alludes to graces received through the intercession of Sister Anna del Salvatore, and asks for prayers to obtain another, promising to name a new work after her.

Company of the Daughters of Mary of Hope

for establishing houses of charity

I M. I.

(Sicily) Comiso, August 26, 1886

Regina Margherita Hospital

Most Reverend Provincial Superior,

Your Ladyship will recall my name, having had the good fortune to meet me in Palermo this past May 4, upon my return from Trapani.

From Your Ladyship I received the precious gift of the handkerchief and hair of Sister Anna del Salvatore; of that blessed soul, from whom I have received special favors. This past June 20, the mere contact of that handkerchief with the dying Giuseppe Presti of Comiso produced a miraculous healing, and I, on the same date, by registered mail, am sending the corresponding packet of attestations and declarations to Rome, to Mother General Gattorno.

In a few days, I shall send you another attestation of a most special grace obtained by contact with those precious hairs.

In giving Your Ladyship such happy news, allow me to remind you of two requests.

1. If you could favor me with some photograph of that generous soul.

2. The Superior of my Company is afflicted with an illness that is beginning to seriously endanger her life. Imagine how grieved my heart is, considering what a storm it would be for me to lose, in the flower of her years, so capable a person, who forms the foundations of my whole Work.

I leave Your Ladyship to consider how desolate I would be, losing the Superior right at the start of the Company's establishment, at the very moment of setting up three other pious houses with several very young Novices; and losing an element who truly seems created by Providence for these Works.

I have placed the Work in the hands of Sister Anna [del Salvatore]. Meanwhile, with all the outpouring of my heart, I beg you and all the Sisters to be so kind as to pray to the blessed soul of Sister A., and to implore from her for me the healing of my Superior. I await this grace from Sister Anna through your intercession and that of the Sisters of your Company.

If Sister Anna grants me this grace, I shall establish a College under her name, and it will be a trumpet of the glories of her virtues.

I remain awaiting your comforting reply, with respect, and I bless you together with the whole Community, and believe me.

Of Your Ladyship.

Sister A. Battistina

Provincial Superior of the

Daughters of St. Anne

Palermo

Your Confrere in Jesus

Canon Gaetano Gagliani

4. Attestation of Giuseppe Presti, of 9/5/1887 (AFSA C.3.163).

He recounts his own healing, after invoking the Servant of God and the contact with one of her relics.

I, the undersigned, declare that, being most gravely ill, with an abscess on my left thigh, so that my recovery seemed almost hopeless, the doctors did not know what to do, seeing me so overcome by pain. Finally, one of the doctors, Professor Romè, decided to operate on me, and indeed it was done, but with no improvement — on the contrary, it got worse.

One day, as the Reverend Father Gagliano happened to pass by with the sisters (collecting alms for the hospital), he came into my house and saw me dying. And behold, Father Gagliano, full of faith, drew out a small portrait of a deceased sister named Sister Anna del Salvatore, and said to me: "Young man, pray with faith to this little nun, for I know most certainly that through her intercession you will obtain the grace of the Most High," and so all knelt and prayed; finally he passed over my face a white handkerchief belonging to the said sister, after which they left.

Meanwhile I kept getting worse, every path of salvation seemed lost, when the Reverend Father Gagliano, after a few days, came a second time, and renewed the same prayer, and so from that day forward I began to improve, so much so that now I am in perfect health, thanks to God, to Mary, and to the intercession of the Sister.

Comiso, September 5, 1887

Giuseppe Presti Rimmaudo

Organist

Concetta Presti, witness

Nunziata Casone, witness

Canon Orazio Callisi, witness

Canon Gaetano Gagliani

5. Attestation of Canon Gaetano Gagliani and his Sisters, of 9/6/1887 (AFSA C.3.163).

The healing of two women, struck down by cholera in a very severe form, is recounted, obtained after they prayed to Sister Anna del Salvatore.

Company of the Daughters of Mary of Hope

for establishing houses of charity

Agira, September 6, 1887

We, the undersigned, swearing upon the Holy Gospel, attest the following.

Cholera having broken out in Agira, we were called to the Ragonese family to attend two cholera victims. We found there the widow Mrs. Scilla and Antonina Ragonese, born Praneta, wife of Professor Luigi Ragonese, both struck by fulminant cholera, in the truly algid stage, such that it allowed not the least hope of survival.

We hastened to encourage the family and the sick women to turn to the holy memory of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, with the certainty of being healed by invoking her with living faith... We placed there the photograph of that blessed soul, and a fervent prayer began... Nothing further was needed. After eight hours, urination resumed, and this twenty minutes after the surgeon, having made his examination, had declared such a manifestation impossible. A notable change for the better began, and within 4 days the sick women left their beds completely healed, with the most vivid conviction of having been healed by Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi.

Canon Gaetano Gagliani

Sister Maria Anna del Salvatore Beda

Sister Ida Avogadro

Sister Diega Tramontana

Sister Antonietta Santorio

Sister Ardica Nunzia

Sister Rosalia Deluca

Sister Venturini Elvira

Sister Giarrizzo Nunzia

Sister Rosa Presti

6. Attestation of Francesco Gagliani, of 9/24/1887 (AFSA C.3.163).

He reports the peace restored to his family after invoking the Servant of God.

Agira, September 24, 1887

I, the undersigned, attest under oath that on September 2, 1887, finding myself beset by a dispute that seriously threatened my family's peace, as soon as I turned for protection to the blessed memory of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, of the Daughters of St. Anne, promising her a Holy Mass, within a few hours I found that matter so resolved that every shadow of dispute vanished, and I returned to tranquility and peace.

In Sister Anna's honor, I issue this statement, written and signed by myself.

Gagliani Francesco, son of the late Dr. Filippo.

7. Attestation of Sfameli Marietta, of 10/6/1887 (AFSA C.3.163).

9. Letter of Sister Anna Quintilla to Rosa Gattorno, of 3/16/1893 (AFSA C.3.163).

She recounts, with many details, the two healings she obtained through the intercession of Sister Anna del Salvatore.

Dearest Mother,

Although your letter required no reply, being rather itself the reply to one of mine, I nonetheless hasten to write to you, first to express my great consolation at the visit paid to you by the Bishop of Como, and with unspeakable joy I sense that our Sisters will also be in Como. Dear Mother, here I am then to give the account of two graces received through our Sister A. del Salvatore.

The first was in 1888, and you yourself, O dear Mother, saw it with your own eyes, that is, on my chest, right side. Yes, one evening, as I was lying down for the night's rest, I felt as though the point of a needle had entered the right side of my chest, and, without knowing the cause, day by day the pain, redness, and swelling grew, to such a point that I could bear it no longer. The Sisters begged me to be seen by a doctor, but I said: no, I will put all my trust in dear Sister A. del Salvatore. Indeed I began a novena to Our Lady, yes, but as intercessor I put Sister A. del Salvatore, and I further placed her portrait over the afflicted spot. Oh, miracle! After twenty days of suffering, which still caused me fever, on the fifth day of the novena, behold, a hole formed through which the point of a pin could pass, and a few drops of blood as black as coal came out, the rest pure water, and day by day the swelling went down and the redness diminished, and finally I was healed without doctors. The purges were without number, but my intestines no longer worked at all. You, O Mother, called me, sent me for some fifteen days to Pisa, and there they no longer knew what more could be done to make my intestines active. I said: no, I will take no medicines. I begin a novena to Sister A. del Salvatore, taking a thread from her stockings by mouth, and behold the second miracle: on the second day of the novena, behold my body set right.

Yes, all this for her Glorification. Bless me, O Mother. Your most affectionate daughter

Sister A. Quintilla C.

17. Reports on the healing obtained by Sister Anna Bertilla Dall'Omo on August 23, 1907 (AFSA C.3.163).

a. Report of the healed woman, of 5/1/1913.

(On the same sheet, as a single document, are the attestations of the Community, of Fr. Fortunato Raffaelli, and of Cardinal Maffi).

She recounts, in detail, her own illness and the prodigious healing obtained during a triduum of prayers offered to obtain the intercession of the Servant of God.

A. M. F.

Account of a healing obtained by the undersigned, unworthy daughter of St. Anne, through the intercession of the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi.

In the month of March of the year 1907, I noticed a slight swelling on the left side of my chest; I paid no attention to it, but it kept growing day by day, slowly, and since I felt no pain I said nothing about it to the Reverend Superior.

In the month of June of the same year I noticed a marked swelling, and, having been prescribed the baths, I went with the Superior to Montecatini, and she, as we were together, since we slept in the same room, noticed the thing, which I wanted to hide, saying it was nothing, but I felt considerable pain; the Superior grew worried; indeed, when the baths were over and we had returned home, she wanted to have me examined, despite much reluctance, which put it off for several days.

Meanwhile the illness progressed in an extraordinary way, and the doctor, Dr. Ettore Paracca, now deceased, was then called; he examined me precisely on the feast of St. Anne, and declared to the Superior and to Sister Anna Tranquillina, the nurse, that it was a malignant cancer. The doctor prescribed me an ointment and said he would return the next day; meanwhile the illness and the infection progressed immeasurably; when the doctor returned, he said the operation was necessary, and that I should continue with the same ointment. How much it pained me! I suffered greatly, and was reduced to the point of being unable to stand. After another ten days had passed, the affected part grew so much that I could no longer remain dressed, and the doctor advised me to support the weight of the swollen part of my chest with a band hung around my neck, and to wear a loose corset; and indeed, this I did, and the Sisters can also attest to this, who saw me go in the morning to the sacristy door to receive Holy Communion.

On August 11, the attending doctor came, and with him the surgeon Professor Noccioli, for a consultation; I was examined by both, and it was confirmed that it was a malignant cancer, and it was decided to perform the operation; but the Professor advised waiting another 18 days. Dr. Paracca and Professor Noccioli went together to the Superior to find the most suitable place in the House to operate on me, and chose the room nearest the church as being airier and closer, so as to carry me back to bed afterwards; moreover, they settled on the sum needed, which was 600 lire, and said that three doctors would come, but they did not fix the day.

I kept getting worse and worse; the Reverend Superior was summoned by the Most Eminent Cardinal, who had learned of the matter from Dr. Paracca, also his physician, who gave her encouragement, since the Reverend Superior was weeping, and he told her he would not allow me to be taken to the hospital, that they must operate on me at home, but said that 1000 lire would not be enough for her. The Reverend Superior also asked for, and obtained from the Reverend Mother General, permission to keep the Blessed Sacrament exposed on the day of the operation. Sister Anna Tranquillina prepared everything necessary for this purpose, and everything was ready. During this time I suffered indescribably, and wished that the day of the operation would come soon; I remained always either in bed or on a couch, unable to stand; a great weight, of about three kilograms, made me lean to the left; Sister Anna Teodora was assigned to assist me during the operation, because Sister Anna Tranquillina said she did not have the courage.

The Most Reverend Father Confessor wished to find out whether I would survive the operation; he spoke with Dr. Paracca, who told him he could not promise it, that it was a most difficult case, that the area would have to be entirely scraped, and there was danger that I would not withstand the chloroform, given my extreme weakness; this same thing the Most Reverend Father Confessor told me when he questioned me to hear my own opinion. Meanwhile August passed, and mid-September arrived. The Reverend Superior was weeping and praying, when a happy thought came to the Most Reverend Canon Fortunato Raffaelli, our officiant and extraordinary confessor, who for a long time had told us he had a special devotion and full trust in the intercession of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, and he said to the Reverend Superior: "What? You have a saint in the Institute, and you grieve so much? Let us begin a Triduum to obtain the grace through the intercession of Sister A. del Salvatore."

No sooner said than done: on the 21st of the same month this Triduum was begun, with the faith that everyone can imagine. On the first day the aforementioned Most Reverend Canon Fortunato Raffaelli celebrated, and recited the prayer composed by our venerated Foundress Mother to the Most Holy Trinity, with the addition of three Glory Be's, for the speedy beatification of Sister Anna del Salvatore, and on this first day I noticed a slight improvement.

On the second day the Most Reverend Father Confessor, Fr. Giosuè Donati, celebrated, and on this day, indeed immediately after Holy Mass, I said I felt much better; I was more relieved and had more strength. The following day the Most Reverend Father Confessor again came to celebrate; when the service was over I at once said to the Reverend Superior: "I am healed, I am healed, I want to get dressed," and I no longer felt any pain at all, and the swelling vanished almost suddenly.

I dressed at once; I had nothing left at all; I myself could not believe it; the Reverend Superior wept with consolation, Sister A. Tranquillina, who had been nursing me, was astonished, and so were all the other Sisters. All at once the news spread outside, and several people came to see me and question me. The Most Eminent Cardinal Archbishop Maffi wished to see me, and as soon as he was before me he exclaimed: "Oh! my graced little Sister, so how are you?" "Well, Your Eminence," I answered, and he rejoiced with me at so great a grace, and to this day, whenever he sees me, he says to me: "my graced little Sister, are you still doing well?"

Dr. Paracca then returned and found me perfectly healed, and said: "The Professor will come." And I answered: "There is no longer any need, because I am well." "It doesn't matter," he added, and indeed Professor Noccioli came, and although he saw me as healthy as I am now, he nonetheless wished to examine me. Hardly believing his own eyes, he examined me first, and then Dr. Paracca, and they found no trace left of the illness, not even the smallest gland, as the said Professor had to admit.

From the time when this happened to now, some six years have passed: I assure you that I have never again felt anything in the affected area. All this is what I can say in plain truth, and I am ready to confirm it, if needed, even under oath.

And in witness, I sign.

Pisa, May 1, 1913

Sister Anna Bertilla Dall'Omo

In witness,

18. Letter of Sister Anna Sista Staffieri to the Superior General Sister Anna Camilla Valentini, of 3/31/1927 (AFSA C.3.163).

My good Mother,

neither I nor any of my Sisters knew Sister A. del Salvatore Orsi; yet I have received from this dear Sister of ours a grace, which I shall now recount.

I do not recall the date well, but it seems to me it was around 1902, when a tumor appeared on my shoulder, which caused me untold suffering, forcing me to stay in bed. The doctor called in declared without further ado that the operation was necessary, to be done after two or three days. Imagine my fright. I at once commended myself to Sister A. del Salvatore and began a triduum with her intercession; I asked the Superior to have the orphans do the same triduum, I applied to my tumor the image of Sister A. del Salvatore, and awaited the grace calmly. On the morning the triduum ended I was completely healed; the doctor came to operate on me, but I went to meet him, telling him I was well. He, not believing it, wanted to examine me, and said that I no longer had anything at all.

Bless me; I kiss the Crucifix and your hand.

Your most affectionate daughter

Sister A. Sista Staffieri

Crispiano, March 31, '27 [1927]

19. Reports concerning the healing of Sister A. Giuseppa Rovello, year 1957 (AFSA C.3.163).

a. Letter of Sister Anna Giuseppa Rovello to Superior General Sister Anna Sebastiana Pifferi, of 1/10/1958.

She gives an account of her healing, obtained by commending herself to the intercession of Sister Anna del Salvatore.

A. M. F.

Account of a grace received through the intercession of the Servant of God Sister A. del Salvatore Orsi.

Most Reverend Mother,

For more than a year I had been suffering pains in my feet that even made me weep! I could not stand at all, so much so that the sisters would sometimes charitably give me their hand to help me walk.

My good Superior, with motherly concern, had me examined by the doctor, who diagnosed that these sufferings were due to the strong quinine I had taken during a bout of malaria a couple of years before; he prescribed me pills and other treatments, always with negative results. Discouraged, I also wrote to you, Most Reverend Mother, letting you know that I could no longer continue in my office of cook, which forced me to stand from morning till night. You answered me in a motherly way that you would pray in a special way for me, to beg the Lord for my healing.

On October 28 of that same year, having learned of the exhumation of the bones of the Servant of God, Sister A. del Salvatore, I asked my good Superior to send me to attend the sacred ceremony; she agreed.

Arriving, as God willed, at the cemetery, I could no longer stand, and how much I had to struggle to be able to enter the chapel, because I was constantly pushed back by a sister in religion who told me: "Where do you think you're going, so fat, nobody can get in here." I pretended not to hear and said to myself: "If I manage to touch the sacred remains of the Servant of God, I will surely be healed." Finally, with the permission of the Reverend Provincial, my turn came to be able to kiss those sacred bones; I did so with all the fervor of faith, and asked for the grace I desired, certain of being heard!

But the next day, in the morning, on getting up, I noticed that the pains had become sharper, with the addition of still others in my shoulders that prevented any movement. Weeping, I turned to the Servant of God, speaking to her with frank familiarity: "Listen, Sister A. del Salvatore, you too were a cook like me, and you know what that office demands: standing from morning till night!... If you want me to go on in the kitchen, you must take away these pains"; I prayed this way for three days; on the third night I dreamed of the Servant of God, much more beautiful than in the photograph, holding a golden heart in her hand, which, showing it to me, she said: "Sister A. Giuseppa, see this heart, open it and take what is inside." In the morning, on rising, to my great amazement, I no longer felt any pain, neither in my feet nor in my shoulders; like a little bird I went to church to thank the Lord for the grace granted through the intercession of Sister A. del Salvatore. Two months and more have already passed, and I feel very well indeed, I fly like an airplane, I carry out my duties without ever feeling the old sufferings again, and I carry my 110 kilograms on my body like a light feather!!

Most Reverend Mother, I would have liked to let you know of the grace received before today, but I was advised to wait some time; now I have decided to make my gratitude towards the Servant of God public; my heart can no longer remain silent!

I ask that you be willing to publish in the "bulletin" the grace received, thus fulfilling the promise made.

With thanks, and devoted affection, I kiss your right hand, asking your blessing.

Most affectionate Daughter

Sister A. Giuseppa Rovello

Palermo, January 10, 1958

Institute for the Blind

b. Account of Sister Anna Amelia Casini, of 3/10/1958.

She recounts her own sudden healing from phlebitis after praying fervently to the Servant of God.

Castiglione di Sicilia (Catania)

I come to report a grace obtained through the intercession of the late Provincial Sister A. del Salvatore Orsi.

In January of this year, I went to my family's home to visit my gravely ill sister. A few days after my arrival, one morning, while getting up to go to my village's nearby church, I noticed that I could not move my left leg; it was swollen and heavy as lead. Despite the seriousness, I wanted to get out of bed to walk; every effort was useless, I could not set my foot on the ground, and it took a great deal to get me back into bed. The family doctor was called, who prescribed hot compresses and plenty of ichthyol on the affected area. At the second visit, which took place after five days, the doctor openly declared that it was phlebitis and that I had to stay a month in bed without moving so as not to cause complications. As soon as the doctor and my relatives left the room, in the dismay in which I found myself, the Provincial, Sister A. del Salvatore, flashed into my mind, and knowing of the many wonders worked for the citizens of Palermo, where her body lies, I prayed to her fervently. I invoked her with such ardor and trust; I spoke to her as though she were present, and asked her to intercede with God for me, at least to be able to walk and soon return to the Community; to the invocation I added 3 Our Fathers, Hail Marys and Glory Be's, promising that I would have the grace published in the "Virga Jesse" bulletin.

Oh, what a great wonder! On the second day of unceasing prayer I had a great improvement; the swelling had disappeared. I got out of bed at once and with immense joy began to walk. On the third day I was already perfectly healed. When the doctor returned, to his great surprise, he attributed the fact to supernatural intervention, and he himself wished to testify to it with a certificate which I attach to this account [cf. no. 20, a.].

My family, too, gives grateful thanks and wishes the grace to be published, and sends 1,000 lire for the expenses of the Cause of Beatification of the Provincial Orsi.

May God be praised for this, and the most worthy religious, Daughter of St. Anne, through whose intercession I returned in excellent health from the distant Tuscan region (Lucca) to beautiful Sicily.

Sister Anna Amelia Casini

Daughter of St. Anne

March 10, 1958

b) From the writings of Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno

a. Excerpts from the Memoirs. Intimate diary of the mystical experiences of Mother Rosa Gattorno. Edition edited by Lázaro Iriarte, OFM Cap., Rome 1996 (AFSA A.2.31; A.2.32; A.2.33; A.3.31; A.3.32; A.3.33).

The foundress Rosa Gattorno held Sister Anna del Salvatore very dear; she turned to her to ask for prayers or to receive advice on various problems, having noticed how the Lord had enriched this daughter of hers with precious charisms, and having seen her advance by great strides along the path of holiness.

After her death, she experienced even more keenly the spiritual closeness and the effective mediation before God of "this friendly soul," to the point that, in every circumstance of particular need, she willingly entrusted herself to her intercession.

Reproduced here, from the printed text, are about 18 excerpts concerning the profound spiritual bond that existed between the Foundress and Sister Anna del Salvatore.

1. News of the death of Sister Anna del Salvatore, June 7, 1885 (pp. 717-718).

The death of Sister Anna del Salvatore is foreshadowed in the Mother by an extraordinary sadness. The Servant of God was endowed in her life with divine lights; she had the gift of prophecy, obtained great graces, lived union with God to a very high degree, and was profoundly humble. The Foundress recalls the hours spent with her in holy conversations; she asks for signs confirming that the light appearing to her is hers.

June 7th: I felt a melancholy, and kept, every so often, growing faint. What can this mean? And then, on the 7th, after dinner, towards evening, there appeared to me a soul flying up to heaven; together with it there was another, as though they were two, or as though it were going to join another [soul]. What this brought upon me I cannot explain. Oh blessed soul, why have you flown so soon to heaven, and left me in a sea of sufferings?

She was my comfort. Oh, how endowed she was with divine lights! She had the gift of prophecy: whatever she asked of the Most Holy Mary was all granted her; her union with God was a great thing. Whatever she had asked for, the answer came at once, and it was never wrong, no. [She had] a profound humility, always considering herself the lowliest of creatures. Oh, how great she was in God's sight! Oh sweet Love!

My dear Sister Anna del Salvatore: [I remember] those long evenings we spent together, always speaking of things [of] our sweet Love. Patience! May the will of my Beloved be done in all things.

While I was praying after holy communion, and this evening for Sister Anna del Salvatore, I asked her to give me a sign that the light circling around me was her, who had gone to Paradise. [I asked] that this sign be clear, like a great provision or some other grace that I had long been asking for. She appeared to me and said to me: "Today this sum will arrive" (as indeed happened); "the grace you desire you will have soon."

And smiling, and raising her hand, she made me a sign of confirmation. I asked her about the health of certain persons, and she told me: "Be at peace, they will always be well."

I had told her that I wanted this other thing as well: that she would come and tell me certain things. She answered me: "I cannot come."

But the reason she did not tell me. In the end, she left me a peace beyond compare.

Oh blessed soul, who have finished suffering so much, and already enjoy the reward of your immense sufferings and anguish! Remember the one you left behind down here!

2. The angelic purity of Sister Anna del Salvatore. Her charity (pp. 722-723).

She receives insights into the grace granted, as to purity, to Sister Anna del Salvatore and to herself. She asks for and obtains the healing of a benefactor. She recalls how in life the Servant of God suffered greatly, but with great charity always wished that everyone be well.

Last night there appeared to me a sash, a little more than a meter long and twenty centimeters wide; it stopped in the air and, as I gazed at it fixedly, behold a voice: "This is the sash I wore, that mark they saw on my heart."

How beautiful was the lesson she gave me! How Jesus had preserved her, through this, from the slightest feeling: her flesh was entirely dead, she understood nothing of what immodesty is, that is, she understood everything and nothing remained with her; she saw the horror of sin and did not know what it meant. Oh, what a mystery she explained to me! Now I understand how great this grace is, and it made me understand the grace I myself have always had, but in a different way: the flesh and senses dead, but the intellect still understood, still grasped the malice of sin.

My God, I am sorry for not having written everything down exactly. Oh, how I remained; but my body was beginning to rise, and my side [to] do as usual already, and so I remained thus drowsy.

Returned to where I was, at the side of my Beloved, I remained wholly in him. Oh dear soul, you have promised me that I will soon have a grace, and I await it!

Last night, as I was praying to this dear little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore, that she would obtain for me the healing of a benefactor who was unwell, shortly after she assured me that he would recover, and showed me that he would not only [recover] but would regain more health than before, and I saw him so robust, calm, and he will live long. I was left so certain of it, and [felt] an inner joy joined to a sense of security...

All doubts and thoughts vanished, so that today I find myself speaking of him this way.

A most beautiful light always circled around me, very beautiful and more shining than when she [Sister A. del Salvatore] died, and greater. I spoke, and it circled rejoicing. Oh dear little daughter!

[I had] certain thoughts while I was in church today: that a person might fall ill with a bad illness. I commended myself to her, and behold she made me see that it would never come, and that it would go elsewhere, so as to do nothing to anyone. Dear soul, while she herself suffered so much and always suffered atrociously, she desired nothing else but that everyone be well and that no one should have to suffer. What boundless charity!

3. The effective intercession of Sister Anna del Salvatore, "a beautiful soul, steeped in charity" (p. 724).

Sister Anna del Salvatore continues to be her comfort and help, as when she was on this earth. She continually questions her, and from her obtains sure answers.

She recalls that she occupied herself with the Institute; she is truly "steeped in charity."

Today was a day of sorrows, and I had only the comfort of my dear Sister Anna del Salvatore, who comforted me in so many things, telling me to be at peace: Oh, the sight of this dear little daughter is such a comfort and help to me! I ask her everything, as when she was here below among us wretched ones. She answers me with broken but certain words, or with signs. [If] there is time she signals it to me by raising a hand, and makes a sign to wait. Oh beautiful soul, steeped in charity! Even now you make this beautiful gift of yours felt all the way from Paradise.

Today I saw that the Rules will soon be approved; oh what consolation! She [knows] everything that happens; yes, how much she concerned herself with the whole Institute! what a dear creature!

4. Effective help from Sister Anna del Salvatore (pp. 727-728).

At the death of Sister Anna del Salvatore she had feared being left without her assistance; instead she receives help from her in an even more effective way; she asks her for many graces and always obtains an answer.

Some days ago I was praying to my dear little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore. Oh what a dear little daughter, and how she assists me! I believed I had lost her, and that I could no longer ask her for a word; but no, she is always with me, and I would say even more than before: I ask her something, and she immediately answers me so clearly that no doubt remains with me, and I at once see the effects. I asked her if she had healed a person who was of such concern to the Institute. She answered me: "She will be very well."

News came that she was healed and was doing very well. For other [graces] of this kind I had an answer. Of one she told me: "For now she will not die, but she will never be healed of this illness again."

I asked her other things and for all of them I had an answer. Thus, for the arrival of the sisters from America, she told me: "Between the fifteenth and the twentieth." [For] another matter [she told me]: "By Saturday."

Lastly, about a grace I was seeking, she answered me nothing, and I asked her about another, which I would have first; she told me [that I would have] the last one I was seeking, and I would have it by the feast of St. Anne:

Oh, how many things I ask of her, and she answers all of them! Oh my dear angel! what days of tribulation!

5. Prophetesses and prophets who err in their predictions (p. 740).

Many people presume to make prophecies to the Mother, but they are mistaken; only those made by Sister Anna del Salvatore, even from when she was alive, have proven true and are coming to pass.

How many prophecies people make to me and write to me, but only one so far I see is coming true, because when [Sister Anna del Salvatore] was alive, how many times I experienced it, and all of them true. How sure my dear Sister Anna del Salvatore was in what she said! Oh, how many things she told me, and other things she wrote to me likewise, and they are coming to pass: but with so many other prophetesses and prophets, I see that my Beloved does not allow them to tell me things as I know they are. Oh, how quickly one can go wrong!

When we want to put something of our own into the things of God, that is when everything remains imperfect.

6. A "lovely contest" with Sister Anna del Salvatore (p. 755).

Sister Anna del Salvatore obtains healing graces, but does not want it known that they happened through her intercession; even in Paradise she wants to remain hidden.

It was a lovely struggle between me and my Sister Anna del Salvatore. I would have liked to see a healing through her, and she [answered me] no. I said to her: "Well then, yes, dear little daughter, at least let this donkey, in the name of her God, see the grace at work; let this creature be healed, and behold the grace is done."

I laughed about it: "Oh dear little daughter, how odd you are, even in Paradise you want to stay hidden!"

For this reason she did not allow it to appear, nor the grace to happen through my own paltry prayers, no! Everything was kept covered, but the scene that took place at that moment...

I saw her so displeased, and she was serious with me: "I do not want it, it must be this way."

I could not help telling her: "How odd you are!"

She had told me that a certain person would give birth to a child on such a day, and then she came to warn me that it was not yet time, that several days were still needed, and made me feel that all would go well.

7. Presentiments and clarifications. From the notes of 1886 (p. 767).

She foresees an earthquake, which will occur in Sicily; but Sister Anna del Salvatore assures the Mother that the sisters will be safe.

Last night, the 8th (...), I saw the scourge that was prepared for Sicily: a terrible earthquake. What sorrow! But my dear little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore, assured me that they would be spared from it, and nothing would happen to them; she urged me to write this to a benefactress437 of the Order, and I did so at once.

8. The continual help of Sister Anna del Salvatore. Notes of 1887 (p. 798).

In the midst of so many sorrows, Sister Anna del Salvatore is her help; she makes herself present promptly, as when she was in this world.

Oh, how clear communication with my dear Sister Anna del Salvatore always is! Oh blessed soul! Whatever I ask of her, she answers me so clearly, and always promptly, as when she was in the world: in such great and continual sorrows as I always find myself in, I can say that it is she who helps me: how many times, weeping, I call upon her, and she... Oh dear little daughter, pray, pray for me!

9. News of the death of St. John Bosco. Notes of the year 1888 (p. 811).

Mother Gattorno writes of having seen a globe of fire in her room, and fears it foretells her own death; she questions Sister Anna del Salvatore, who answers her clearly that this fire foretells the death of Don Bosco.

January 31st [1888]: I was unwell all day; in the evening I truly felt the pains of purgatory.

At eleven o'clock a light, like an oval fire, stood fixed on the wall of the room. I looked at it and asked who it was and what it meant; a trembling came over me, [as] if it signified my end, not because I felt any sorrow or fear of it, no, but all of a sudden how do I leave [everything]? If it were true I could prepare myself...

...A whisper made me reflect, and I remembered that the globe was that same [sign], and it kept repeating in my mind; I commended my soul and asked my Sister Anna del Salvatore insistently to tell me whether it was I, or who it was. She told me firmly that it was Don Bosco, and that I should not think of dying at all, no. She grew [quite] cross: "It is not her, it is Don Bosco!"

10. At the tomb of Sister Anna del Salvatore. The good spirit of the Sisters of Sicily: notes of the year 1889 (pp. 954-955).

She experiences ineffable feelings at the tomb of Sister Anna del Salvatore. She entrusts to her intercession the sisters of Sicily, that they may keep up the good spirit and obtain the spirit of charity and self-denial.

I wish I could describe what I felt at the tomb of my dear little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore! Oh dear soul, pray much for me and for the sisters of Sicily! I can say that she truly does so, because I see in these creatures a good spirit, and they are all eager to work for the glory of God.

I found good souls; it is true that one always tries to place the best ones there, but how can one tell? Unless there is a hand guiding them and giving them a spirit of charity and self-denial...

11. Comforted by Sister Anna del Salvatore. From the notes of 1890 (pp. 969-970).

In so many sorrows of spirit, the presence of Sister Anna del Salvatore is a relief to Mother Gattorno. She assures her that a sick person close to her will not die; she instills in her confidence and courage in her actions.

[...] But today I see it is changing, and it seems to me my condition is returning; to suffer much, but not torments to the point of feeling myself faint. Thus I still always see my infamies in my examinations, but I pray with peace and resignation, and do not feel myself tormented. My little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore, in this state was a true relief to me, because, when I did not understand who that person was who was [to] die, feeling somewhat unwell, and fearing that she might be taken from me, I would ask her about it. She always answered me, assuring me to be at peace, that nothing would happen. How she set my mind at rest!

So too for certain other actions she encouraged me. [I had] a certain fear of passing away at any moment; she assured me it would not happen. Oh what comfort, my dear little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore!

12. The help of Sister Anna del Salvatore (pp. 1029-1030).

During the night Sister Anna del Salvatore was a great comfort to her; she reassures her in her agitations and instills peace in her.

[I will say] a word about my dear little daughter, who last night was my help, my relief; she calmed me in my agitations [from the fear] of having something I could not withstand; I would not otherwise have been able to continue my retreat. Dear angel, what comfort!

[She was always] ready to answer me: "My Salvatore, will it be this or that?" "Not at all" - she would answer me.

"Poor me, I feel so unwell!" And she told me to be calm, that it would pass. Oh, how it comforted me!

13. The healing of a sister obtained by Sister Anna del Salvatore (pp. 1035-1036).

During the night she asks Sister Anna del Salvatore for the healing of a sick Daughter of St. Anne who suffers greatly, and obtains it. It is a great miracle. The Servant of God prays continually for the Institute she loves. Jesus denies her no grace asked for the Institute.

Oh, what a night! I could no longer close my eyes; tired, I felt myself growing faint, and I prayed for a grace that so weighed on my mind, for a poor Daughter of St. Anne who was suffering so much: I asked my Sister Anna del Salvatore, and she answered me: "It is all over, she is well, it is nothing." "But how? The doctors say it will take so much longer to heal!" "Not at all, it is all over:"

Today she writes to me that it is all over and that she is healed. Oh, for me it was a true miracle, a very great grace that dear Sister Anna del Salvatore obtained from God! She is a comfort to me amid so many sorrows; she [speaks] always a word of peace, [gives] a suggestion. In the end, when I ask her, she answers me whether I should do it or not, as always. She loves the Institute, and all her prayers are for it. Oh, truly, more and more I come to know what a beautiful soul she is, and what she wants she obtains [from] Jesus! She can refuse nothing to her Institute, it is plain to see.

14. Apprehensions and fears. The answer of Sister Anna del Salvatore (pp. 1043-1044).

After the thanksgiving following Communion, she questions Sister Anna del Salvatore about many things, and receives from her clear and thorough answers, both regarding the Institute and her own person. She also shares her sorrow over the illness of her son Alessandro.

August 12th. For several days I kept meaning to write, but time was lacking to me, and my poor health... At night writing is so wearisome for me, because my poor head is worn out from the day's work. As tonight, which is already late, but I feel a strong urge to write, believing this to be the will of my God. I put off going to bed and set myself to tell, as best I can, what has happened to me these past days.

...Yesterday, then, and I still hold so vividly in my mind what I had after my thanksgiving, I needed to know many things. I took [courage] to ask my little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore, and how well she answered me!

I wanted to know whether my letter sent to a Cardinal had been accepted. How she comforted me, telling me he desired it and would answer me! Then I asked her so many things, and she answered me so clearly. I went so far as to ask whether my swelling would go down: "Yes" - she answered me - "it will go down."

As for poor Alessandro, oh, how sad she was! She certainly shares my sorrow with me; how I feel it! it is truly intense!

15. Other answers of Sister Anna del Salvatore (pp. 1045-1046).

After the thanksgiving following Communion, she questions Sister Anna del Salvatore about the answer she is awaiting from the Cardinal Protector. She also asks for an explanation of the sadness she feels; the Servant of God foretells that she will have to face a grave sorrow, the content of which she cannot reveal to her.

August 13th. What a terrible night I passed! [...]

This morning, after my thanksgiving, while praying, I felt a kind of deep sadness, always accompanied by dread. But I wanted to persuade myself of this. Who could have left this with me during the night?

But no! I at once set myself to question my dear little daughter, Sister Anna del Salvatore.

First I asked her whether the Cardinal had answered my [letter]. She, kindly, but not as on other occasions, told me yes, that I would soon have it, and that he had read it with pleasure. Then I went on to ask the meaning of that ugly beast. She answered me that I would have to suffer a great sorrow, and, weeping, told me that this would be like a knife that would pierce my chest with grief. She, weeping, comforted me.

"But what will it be?" - I said to her. She answered me that she could not tell me, and that she would pray for me, since in her honor and glory I had made holy communion. [...]

How comforting that dear creature [Sister Anna del Salvatore] is to me! In everything I question her, and she answers me so well, and never gets a single one wrong: from what I could see, from her weeping, and from being unable to tell me anything... And what did I do? I asked her whether it was something concerning the Institute, and I saw there was a great mixture [of things]. I hope God gives me strength, because I already see he is preparing me for it as I said above. It is hard [the suffering] of waiting without knowing what it will be. My Love, have mercy, sweet Jesus!

16. Answers obtained from Sister Anna del Salvatore. From the notes of 1890/91 (pp. 1073-1074).

Sister Anna del Salvatore, when questioned, gives her news of the graces she will obtain; she is always her comfort. She also foretells to her the death of a person.

When this passage ended, I was startled, and no longer savored that union. So I asked the dear Sister Anna del Salvatore to tell me when a person who was expected would arrive. She answered me: "Monday."

So I asked her other things this morning; I asked when I would obtain a grace, and she answered me — I cannot now recall the exact wording — that it had already been granted. I only had to be told of it.

"And the other one?" — I answered — "That too is granted, but it will be communicated to you after a third [grace]."

I have been asking for it for years, and as to this one she answered me that there was still nothing yet, that I would have it too, but that it would still take long.

So I understood that this I would have, but in time, and she made me feel what it would be like once it was done, and so to speak I did not yet possess it. Ah, how orderly, how sweet, my Love, is all that is yours!

Other things I asked her, and in everything I had an answer. How comforting it was to me! [...]

How many things I have had these days, above all of communication with my dear Sister Anna del Salvatore! Oh, truly I can say that she is my comfort!

Now she tells me that M. T. will die. I wish she would tell me whether it will be while traveling, but on this she tells me nothing. [I asked for] the conversion of a sinner, and she did not even say: "Not at all."

Oh, how sure her word is! I would have much to say.

17. Always trusting in the answers of Sister Anna del Salvatore. Years 1891/92 (pp. 1079; 1099; 1155-1156).

Sister Anna del Salvatore confirms to the Foundress that a person will die, and that the difficulties with her brother will be smoothed over. What she told her about the Cardinal Protector proves entirely fulfilled. She reassures her about the danger of a house in Rome being closed.

August 7th. My Sister Anna del Salvatore told me this morning that a person, M. F., will no longer recover, and, questioned about a lawsuit that was to be brought, that is, that my brother wanted to bring against me, she told me that a settlement would be reached; I questioned her about other things, and I was consoled. Blessed soul! I say consoled, because the Lord's Work will gain advantages and greater glory from it. [...]

My Salvatore indeed was not mistaken about the Cardinal Protector. Oh, how good he is to the Lord's Work! A true protector, holy and learned, so enlightened, who has already done much good and continually does for the Lord's Work.

Your words, my little daughter: "He will be the Protector, Cardinal Verga, and he will do great good for the Lord's Work." Blessed are you! [...]

I feared that a house here in Rome might be closed, and I prayed to my Salvatore about it; at once she told me firmly no, that it would not be closed.

After this [happened], the order came to close it, [but she] again [told me]: "No, it will not be closed at all." "Then am I mistaken?" — [I said].

By a coincidence it was left open, and everything was settled. Oh, how many things she told me! [...] I consult her about everything, and always get answers, even about how I should conduct myself. Oh, my Angel!

18. Journey from Florence to Rome. Notes of 1893/94 (pp. 1166-1167).

In her hesitation over delaying her departure, Sister Anna del Salvatore urges the Mother to follow the impulse she felt, foretelling to her the need for her presence in Rome and assuring her a safe journey.

October 2, 1893. I found myself in Florence, and the day before I felt a strong voice telling me: "Go to Rome."

...They announced to us that the train would be greatly delayed. [We thought] an hour, a small matter, but after half an hour our other companions came to us saying that the delay was three hours. My God, what to do? [Someone] urged me to go back home, that we could leave again the next day. [I was] so torn by the thought that the night's steamer passage would be lost, and everything frightened me. I turned to my Sister Anna del Salvatore, my helping angel, and said to her: "What should I do?" She answered me plainly: "Go, there are serious things in Rome, go!" "Alas, is [there] someone ill?" "No," she answered me, "other things."

[When she had] finished saying this, behold they brought me a telegram in which the lawyer told me to go immediately to Rome, as I had to urgently sign a power of attorney. Oh holy soul! I asked her to tell me whether I would have a good journey; she told me yes, that it would be good, and so it was.

b. Excerpts from the Letters of Mother Rosa Gattorno to Emilia Settimo, Princess of Fitalia438; unpublished (AFSA C.1.134/9; C.1.134/10; C.1.135/1; C.135/4; C.1.135/5).

Sharing with her even extraordinary events, Rosa Gattorno writes to this spiritual daughter (who also became her confidante after the death of Sister Anna del Salvatore) 460 letters (at least those that have been found).

Excerpts from 20 letters are selected here, in which Blessed Rosa Gattorno pauses to speak of Sister A. del Salvatore, reporting news of graces, of prodigious interventions that occurred through her intercession, and explicitly attesting to the reputation for holiness attributed to her.

Oh! sweetest love, consume my dear Emilia with the fire of your Farewell, a respectful greeting to the Prince, your excellent consort, and you, dear little daughter, receive a strong embrace in my dear Crucifix from your Ever-faithful.
